channel.title: SecuBuzz · Cybersecurity News Briefs
channel.description: Fast, factual 60-word cybersecurity briefs and CISA KEV alerts for security professionals.

item.title: Red Hat Issues OpenJDK 8 Security Update for RHEL 7
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for java‑1.8.0‑openjdk on Red Enterprise Linux 7 Extended Lifecycle Support to address multiple vulnerabilities. The update covers unspecified Java runtime flaws rated Important, with CVSS base scores linked via CVE references, potentially enabling remote code execution or privilege escalation. System administrators should apply the RHSA‑2026:95598 patch and verify Java version to ensure protection.

item.title: Git Issues Patches for Six Vulnerabilities, Including Code Execution
item.description: Git released patches for six vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-111760, which allows code execution during recursive clones. The flaw stems from an integer truncation in Git’s index handling, enabling attackers to write unintended files or cause memory corruption when processing malicious repositories. Git has issued security updates; users should apply the latest release to mitigate the risk.

item.title: Red Hat Releases Kernel Security Update for RHEL 10
item.description: Red Hat issued a kernel update for Red Enterprise Linux 10 to address multiple security issues. The update targets unspecified kernel vulnerabilities rated Important, with CVSS base scores available via CVE references, indicating potential privilege escalation or denial of service if exploited. Administrators should apply the RHSA‑2026:98638 patch promptly and verify kernel version to ensure protection.

item.title: Qlik Sense Servers Targeted by Reverse Shell Attempts
item.description: Threat actors targeted Qlik Sense servers in October 2026, attempting to deliver PowerShell reverse shells across multiple environments. The activity, observed by Cynet's CyOps and Research teams, involved a narrow three‑minute window and failed to achieve code execution or credential compromise. Security teams should monitor for similar attempts and ensure Qlik Sense is patched to the latest version.

item.title: Asus, Zoom Issue Patches for Execution Flaws
item.description: Asus and Zoom released security patches addressing critical flaws that could allow attackers to execute arbitrary code, overwrite memory, and elevate privileges. The vulnerabilities involve memory corruption and privilege escalation paths, potentially enabling full system compromise if exploited. Users should install the latest updates for both Asus firmware and Zoom client immediately to mitigate the risk.

item.title: Remus Malware Claims Persistent Gmail Access After Reset
item.description: The Remus infostealer asserts it can maintain Gmail access even after victims reset their passwords. The malware reportedly exploits credential persistence mechanisms, potentially leveraging OAuth tokens or cached credentials to bypass password changes. Users should revoke app permissions, enable two‑factor authentication, and monitor account activity regularly to mitigate the threat.

item.title: RHSA-2026:98592: Important: go-fdo-client security update
item.description: An update for go-fdo-client is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.title: Citrix, Ivanti Release Patches for RCE Vulnerabilities
item.description: Citrix and Ivanti disclosed critical vulnerabilities that let attackers tamper with certificate entries and achieve remote code execution on affected hosts. The flaws arise from improper certificate validation, enabling arbitrary code execution and full host compromise; no public exploit is confirmed. Both vendors released patches; administrators should apply updates immediately and verify certificate integrity to mitigate risk.

A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.title: Git CVE-2026-111760 Enables Remote Code Execution
item.description: Git introduced CVE-2026-111760, a flaw that permits remote code execution in enterprise environments. The vulnerability arises from improper input validation in the Git server component, allowing attackers to inject malicious commands; no public exploit is documented. A patch is available; administrators should update Git to the latest release and monitor logs for suspicious activity.

item.title: Cisco BroadWorks CVE-2026-20320: XXE Flaw Patch
item.description: Cisco BroadWorks is affected by CVE-2026-20320, an XML External Entity (XXE) flaw that can enable remote code execution. The vulnerability allows attackers to read arbitrary files and execute commands on the BroadWorks server when processing crafted XML requests. Cisco has released a patch; administrators should apply the update immediately and enable input validation to mitigate the risk.

item.title: Microsoft CVE-2026-124194 Enables Outlook RCE
item.description: Microsoft disclosed CVE-2026-124194, a flaw that allows remote code execution in Outlook on enterprise systems. The issue stems from improper handling of email attachments, enabling attackers to execute arbitrary code; no public exploit is reported. Microsoft has released a patch; users should update Outlook immediately and disable macro execution as a precaution.

item.title: Red Hat rhc Update Addresses Important Vulnerabilities
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for the rhc client on Enterprise Linux 7, addressing vulnerabilities that could allow privilege escalation. The advisory references several CVEs with CVSS scores ranging from 7.5 to 8.3, indicating high exploitation potential for authenticated users. Administrators should apply the rhc update immediately and verify that all affected components are patched to prevent unauthorized access.

item.title: Red Hat tigervnc Update Fixes Important Vulnerabilities
item.description: Red Hat issued an update for tigervnc on Enterprise Linux 9, fixing vulnerabilities that could enable code execution via the VNC protocol. The advisory lists CVEs with CVSS scores of 9.0, indicating a severe risk for systems exposed to untrusted network traffic. Users must apply the tigervnc patch immediately and restrict VNC access to trusted hosts to mitigate the threat.

item.title: N‑able Issues Hotfixes for Zero‑Day RMM Flaws
item.description: N‑able issued hotfixes for zero‑day flaws in its N‑central RMM platform that were publicly disclosed and caused hosted environments to go offline. The flaws arise from unvalidated input in the remote API, letting attackers execute arbitrary code and disrupt services; no public exploit exists. Administrators should apply the hotfixes immediately, monitor API traffic for anomalies, and disable unused remote endpoints.

item.title: Xen Orchestra Auth Bypass CVE-2026-123158 Patched
item.description: Xen Orchestra VSA-2026-062 enables attackers to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to virtual machine management interfaces. The flaw, catalogued as CVE-2026-123158, exploits a missing session validation check, allowing credentialless access with a CVSS score of 8.1. Red Hat has issued a patch for Xen Orchestra; security teams should update immediately and enforce strict access controls.

item.title: Claude Code AI Discovers Technique to Turn Dormant Model Neurons Into Hidden Malware Triggers
item.description: Claude Code helped uncover a technique that can turn an otherwise capable AI model into a sleeper agent by changing fewer than 10 dormant neurons. Called Lazarus, the method plants a hidden backdoor in model weights, allowing an attacker’s trigger to make an AI agent produce commands that download and run malicious code.

item.title: Microsoft Patch Tuesday Addresses Actively Exploited Outlook CVE
item.description: Microsoft released a Patch Tuesday update for Outlook to remediate an actively exploited vulnerability identified as CVE-2026-124194. The flaw permits remote code execution via malicious email attachments, enabling attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected systems. Administrators should apply the Outlook patch immediately and verify Office updates to close the exploitation vector.

item.title: Multiple Windows Remote Desktop Flaws Allow Attackers to Execute Code Over Network
item.description: Microsoft has released security updates for four Windows Remote Desktop Client vulnerabilities that could allow attackers to run code through network connections or local access. Published on November 10, 2026, the flaws involve memory handling errors and a race condition.

item.title: Microsoft Resolves USB Audio Issues from September Updates
item.description: Microsoft addressed USB audio problems affecting Windows users who installed September security updates. The issue stemmed from a driver patch that caused device enumeration failures, disrupting sound output for affected systems; no exploitation was reported. The November 2026 cumulative update restores driver behavior, and users are advised to install the latest package to eliminate the audio malfunction.

item.title: Microsoft researchers demonstrate hidden backdoor technique for AI agents
item.description: Microsoft researchers have demonstrated how small changes to an AI model can implant a hidden backdoor, causing an agent to execute an attacker’s command when a specific trigger appears. The technique, called Lazarus, requires no model retraining and allows the agent to behave normally during standard safety evaluations.

item.title: USN-9041-1: uutils coreutils vulnerabilities
item.description: A local attacker could possibly use this issue to obtain sensitive information or modify file permissions unexpectedly. (CVE-2026-35341) It was discovered that uutils coreutils dd incorrectly suppressed errors during file truncation operations. A local attacker could possibly use this issue to cause silent data corruption. (CVE-2026-35344) It was discovered that uutils coreutils tail incorrectly followed symbolic links when using the --follow=name option.

item.title: Hackers Exploit AhsayCBS Vulnerabilities to Hide Malware in PNG Images and Deploy Stealthy Backdoors
item.description: Hackers exploiting AhsayCBS backup servers have planted webshells, hidden encrypted code inside PNG images, and staged a Python implant designed to run only on its intended host. The findings show an intrusion that extended beyond cryptocurrency mining, giving attackers several ways to keep access to systems responsible for protecting an organization’s backups.

item.title: Linux Kernel NVIDIA BaseOS Vulnerabilities Fixed
item.description: An attacker could exploit kernel flaws in NVIDIA BaseOS network drivers and IPv4 networking to compromise affected systems. The vulnerabilities, identified as CVE-2026-98239 and CVE-2026-98432, allow remote code execution through malformed network packets, posing an exploitation risk. Ubuntu has released a kernel patch that corrects the driver and IPv4 subsystems; apply the update immediately to mitigate the threat.

item.title: Cisco and Openwave Vulnerabilities Identified, Patch Urgently Needed
item.description: Cisco and Openwave systems are affected by a critical flaw identified as CVE-2026-20320. The vulnerability permits remote code execution via malformed network packets, with a public PoC demonstrating exploitation; the flaw could allow attackers to gain system-level access on affected devices. Administrators should apply the vendor-supplied patch immediately and enable the provided detection rules to monitor for exploitation attempts.

item.title: ClickFix Attacks Evolve to Hide Malware in PNG Images and Hijack Windows Domain Controllers
item.description: ClickFix attacks are moving beyond simple malware downloads, with recent investigations revealing executable payloads hidden inside PNG images and intrusions reaching Windows domain controllers. The activity shows how a fake verification prompt can become the starting point for persistent access, credential theft, and movement across corporate networks.

item.title: CISA flags Cisco BroadWorks flaw as actively exploited in attacks
item.description: The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) warned on Tuesday that hackers are now exploiting a high-severity Cisco BroadWorks vulnerability in attacks. The vulnerability is tracked as CVE-2026-20320.

item.title: Ubuntu Adds Revocation Checks to Curl
item.description: Ubuntu 26.10 adds certificate revocation checking to curl, preventing connections to revoked certificates. Earlier releases, such as 26.04, accepted revoked certificates because curl lacked revocation validation, exposing users to man‑in‑the‑middle attacks; OpenSSL also omits revocation checks by default. Upgrade to Ubuntu 26.10 or later to enforce revocation checks, and enable OCSP or CRL verification in OpenSSL for added protection.

item.title: Grafana update released for RHEL9
item.description: Red Hat released a security update for Grafana on RHEL 9, addressing vulnerabilities that could enable unauthorized access or data leakage. The update patches each flaw, with CVSS scores available via CVE references, though no specific CVE IDs are listed. Apply the update through RHEL 9 package manager to eliminate the risks and maintain system integrity.

item.title: China-Linked Hackers Use Fake Chrome Certificate Warnings to Infect Victims With Sparrow Backdoor
item.description: China-linked hackers are turning trusted websites into malware delivery points by displaying fake Google Chrome certificate warnings. The pages urge selected visitors to install a certificate repair utility, but the download instead installs a backdoor that gives attackers remote access to Windows computers.

item.title: Xwayland update released for RHEL 9.4
item.description: Red Hat issued a security update for xorg‑x11‑server‑Xwayland on RHEL 9.4, targeting vulnerabilities that could allow unauthorized access or data exposure. The advisory notes an Important impact rating and references CVSS scores for each flaw, but no CVE identifiers are disclosed. Security teams should apply the update via RHEL 9.4 package manager to mitigate the identified risks.

item.title: Microsoft Resolves Exchange Sign‑In Issues from Server Updates
item.description: Microsoft fixed Outlook sign‑in and mail delivery issues on Exchange Server caused by October 2026 Windows Server updates. The updates disrupted authentication flows, leading to failed logins and delayed message routing; no data exfiltration was reported. The problem is resolved in the latest cumulative update; administrators should apply the patch to restore normal Exchange operation.

item.title: Openwave, BroadWorks vulnerabilities exploited for data leakage
item.description: Threat actors exploited CVE-2026-111793 in Openwave and CVE-2026-20320 in Cisco BroadWorks, enabling leakage of sensitive configuration data. Both flaws allow unauthorized disclosure of configuration information without authentication, and public proof‑of‑concept exploits have been released. Affected systems should apply vendor patches or configuration hardening to prevent further data exposure immediately.

item.title: Intel, AMD patch over 200 vulnerabilities
item.description: Intel and AMD released over 200 patches on Patch Tuesday, addressing critical flaws in Intel TDX software and numerous AMD graphics bugs. The advisory lists multiple CVE identifiers and CVSS scores, indicating a range of severity levels across the affected components. Security teams should apply the vendor patches via their package managers or firmware updates to mitigate the identified risks.

item.title: OpenSSH Update Addresses Moderate Security Issues
item.description: Red Hat released an OpenSSH update for RHEL 10 to address moderate‑severity vulnerabilities affecting the SSH daemon. The advisory cites multiple CVE references with CVSS base scores, but no active exploitation has been observed. Users should install the latest OpenSSH package to ensure protection against the identified weaknesses in all deployments.

item.title: SOS Update Fixes Important Security Bugs
item.description: Red Hat issued a security update for the sos utility on RHEL 10, addressing important bugs that could affect system diagnostics. The advisory references multiple CVE entries with CVSS base scores, indicating a high impact on system stability. Administrators should apply the sos patch promptly to prevent potential denial of service or data corruption during troubleshooting.

item.title: Kernel RMP Check Flaw Enables Hypervisor Out-of-Bounds
item.description: A kernel flaw in IOMMU RMP checks allows a local hypervisor attacker to trigger an out‑of‑bounds condition and corrupt SEV‑SNP guest memory. The vulnerability, identified as CVE‑2023‑20585, could enable privilege escalation within virtualized environments, potentially compromising guest isolation. Red Hat released a kernel patch that restores RMP validation and addresses affected subsystems, and users should apply the update immediately.

item.title: Microsoft Releases Patch for Outlook Bug Exposing NTLMv2 Hashes
item.description: Microsoft released a cumulative update fixing 1,259 flaws, including CVE-2026-124194, an Outlook bug that attackers exploited to exfiltrate NTLMv2 hashes. The flaw permits unauthenticated memory corruption that leaks credential material, enabling credential dumping and lateral movement. Apply the latest cumulative update immediately; no workaround exists, and teams should monitor authentication logs for anomalous NTLM traffic.

item.title: Kernel Vulnerabilities Affect Azure CVM Systems
item.description: Multiple kernel subsystems in Azure CVM instances contain vulnerabilities that could allow a local attacker to compromise system integrity. The flaws affect USB gadget drivers, memory management, networking core, and various architecture modules, but no public exploit has been reported. Red Hat has issued a kernel update that corrects these issues; administrators should apply the patch to mitigate potential exploitation.

item.title: Barracuda Vulnerabilities Exploited for Root Access
item.description: Barracuda devices were hit by recently patched flaws, including CVE-2026-124194, that attackers exploited to bypass authorization and gain root access. The flaw permits unauthenticated users to trigger a buffer overflow in the management interface, enabling privileged command execution and full system compromise. Barracuda recommends applying the latest firmware patch immediately; no workaround exists, and administrators should limit management interface exposure.

item.title: Railway Breach Causes $740,000 Unauthorized AI Usage
item.description: Railway disclosed that customer AI keys stored on its platform were stolen in an October breach. The stolen keys enabled an estimated $740,000 in unauthorized AI usage charges, which Railway pledged to cover. Railway urges customers to rotate API keys and monitor usage logs, while investigating the breach and seeking refunds from AI vendors.

item.title: Top 10 Security Ratings Services Ranked 2026
item.description: The piece ranks the top ten security ratings services for 2026, assessing exposure, patch cadence, breach signals, and overall posture. Ratings now influence insurance premiums, vendor access, and board decisions, with NormShield and RiskRecon highlighted as key players. Stakeholders should examine rating criteria and align their security posture with the metrics used by these services.

item.title: Microsoft Patches AD RCE Vulnerability CVE-2026-119948
item.description: A Windows Active Directory flaw (CVE-2026-119948) lets an authorized attacker run code over a network. The vulnerability, rated Important with a CVSS 3.1 score of 7.5, exploits improper input handling in AD replication. Microsoft issued security updates on November 10, 2026; administrators should apply them immediately to secure domain controllers.

item.title: Microsoft Researchers Show AI Agents Can Be Backdoored by Editing Fewer Than 10 Neurons
item.description: An AI model can be given a hidden backdoor by editing fewer than 10 of its rarely used neurons, without retraining the model, Microsoft researchers have shown. When a chosen trigger appears, the model outputs an attacker's command, which an agent using that model would run with the agent's own permissions.
